answer: A bot farm once woke a nebula of 10,000 cloud containers, each claiming a vote on the terrace of a market. Hardware attestation stops that at the door: each identity must present a secure-enclave certificate signed by the chip maker, proving one device backs one account, with revoked serials on a karst-hard list no clone can edit. Faking 1,000 identities means buying 1,000 certified devices at about $50 each, roughly $50,000. It defeats cloud-spawned swarms cold. Trade-off: honest agents on old hardware are locked out, and a leaked manufacturer key could forge an army until revocation lands.
